VEHICLES -- BRAKE LININGS
SHEAR STRENGTH METHOD OF TEST

INTERNAL

1 SCOPE This standard specifies the method of measllring the internal shear strength ( stress ) of brake lining materials for disc brake pads and drum brake linings used in automotive vehicle brakes. 2 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of the definitions shall apply. 2.1 Internal It is ratio area. 2.2 Shear Shear of Force to the lining or pad, which ( see Fig. 1 ). the standard the following

3 TEST

APPARATUS

3.1 The apparatus comprises of a tensile or compression test machine and it shall be equipped with a fixture to apply the required load in the prescribed manner. The test machine shall be provided with an arrangement to register or record the load at shear. 3.2 The rate of loading shall be controlled such a way that the load iacreases with average rate of 4 500 -& 500 N/s. in un

Strength shear force to the stressed

The force vertical causes the shearing

3.3 It is further recommended that the unit controllrng the rate of load functions in such a way that instantaneous rate is within the limits of 4 500 f 2 250 N/s, when the shear force is above 5 000 N. NOTE - In the case of hydraulically
sile or comrression test machines

operated tenthe requirements

SHEAR

FORCE

&m,

may be met by setting the unloaded movement of the piston. The rate of speed, in mm/s, depends on the type of machine. 3.4 The fixture ( see Fig. 1 ) shall consist of two blocks, which slide with as little friction as possible against one another, with a maximum movement of O-1 mm. The friction between the block and the guide shall be minimal or capable of being recorded so that an allowance may be made in calculating the applied load. The blocks shall be grooved to receive the specimen. The specimen shall fill the grooves completely to prevent tilt under load. 3.4.1 It is essential that the shear force is applied through the centre of fixture and specimen and parallel to the guide within O,l mm at a length of 100 mm. 4 TEST PROCEDURE

4.1 Place the specimen in the fixture and gradually increase the load in a direction parallel to the direction of stress at normal service conditions. 4.2 The load shall not be applied in shocks and the rate of increase shall be as specified in 3.2 and 3.3. 4.3 The test shall be carried out till the breaking up of the lining material occurs. 1
